prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-20, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-20):
| Current ratio           | 1.30 |
| Retained earnings       | 33,239M |
| Current liabilities     | 13,326M |
| Current assets          | 17,271M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 29,093M |
| Total liabilities       | 43,439M |
| Total assets            | 73,680M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,498M |
| Revenue                 | 34,015M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows moderate leverage with total liabilities around 43.4B against equity 29.1B and assets 73.7B, yielding a debt-to-equity dynamic around 1.5x. Liquidity is decent (current ratio 1.30) and EBIT margin is modest (~4.4%), but interest coverage is uncertain given limited earnings relative to high leverage, suggesting some default risk could emerge in downturns. Overall credit risk appears within the lower investment-grade range, but not strongly protected, supporting a BBB rating.

DECISION: BBB
